fixes.fix: <jp reading="てんきよほうによると、こんしゅうはあめつづきだそうだ">天気予報によると、今週は雨続きだそうだ</jp><text> (Segundo a previsão do tempo, esta semana vai ser de chuva atrás de chuva.)</text>
fixes.why:
Complaint confirmed. 世の中 is 'a sociedade, o mundo das pessoas, os tempos' (exactly how this lesson's own list glosses it), never a geographic area, so 天気予報によると、世の中は雨続きだ is unnatural Japanese and the gloss 'o mundo todo' teaches the wrong sense. The replacement uses 今週 as the topic and closes 〜によると with そうだ, the hearsay ending the pattern requires. No 。 at the end, per the house rule for generated Japanese. 世の中 keeps its definition in the vocabulary list; several other words in that same list (予防, 離婚, 嫁, 陸) also have no example sentence, so the lesson stays consistent. A separate 世の中 example was not added because that would insert a new

fixes.current: O verbo da ação fica sempre na forma de dicionário antes de
fixes.fix: O verbo da ação fica na forma de dicionário (ordem positiva) ou na forma ～ない (ordem negativa) antes de
fixes.why: Complaint confirmed: the l1-pitfall note states the action verb is ALWAYS in dictionary form before ように, which contradicts the paragraph two blocks above (医者はお酒を飲まないように言いました), exercise 1 (answer ない) and the lesson's own checklist item mentioning ～ないように. fixes.current: MESMO que o verbo final seja educado (</text><jp>頼まれた</jp><text>, "fui pedido")
fixes.fix: MESMO que o verbo final seja educado (</text><jp>頼まれました</jp><text>, "me pediram")
fixes.why: Two confirmed defects in one span. 'Fui pedido' is not grammatical pt-BR (pedir does not passivize with the asked person as subject); the natural gloss is 'me pediram', which is exactly what exercise 2 and exercise 5 of this same lesson already use. And 頼まれた is the plain past passive, so labelling it 'educado' is wrong; 頼まれました is the polite form and matches the example 手伝ってくれと頼まれました three lines above. Keeping 'educado' preserves the concessive contrast the sentence is built on (brusque くれ inside the quote versus a polite reporting verb outside). Tag multiset identical before and after: </text>, <jp>, </jp>, <text>.

The complaint is real: standard kanji usage assigns 測る to size/length, 量る to weight and 計る to time/quantity, so サイズを計る in ex:n3-relato-06-5 is nonstandard in a lesson whose whole point is that the kanji decides the meaning. But it cannot be repaired inside exercises[4].answer alone. The prompt says 'Traduza para o japonês: ''Me pediram que medisse o tamanho.'' (use 計る e a gramática てくれと)', the explanation says '計る (はかる) é medir', and the lesson body and unlocks list carry vocab:計る. Changing only answer.text and answer.accept to 測って would grade a learner wrong for typing exactly what the prompt told them to use. A human must choose one of two coordinated rewrites: keep 計る and move the object to a time target (prompt to 'Me pediram que cronometrasse o tempo', answer.text to 時間を計ってくれと言われた, accept and explanation to match), or keep サイズ and switch prompt, answer, accept, explanation and the vocab tie-in to 測る. The same edit is needed in course/n3/topic-48-relato/lesson-06.json. fixes.current: <jp reading="ふっていないうちに">降っていないうちに</jp>
fixes.fix: <jp reading="あめがふらないうちに">雨が降らないうちに</jp>
fixes.why: Complaint confirmed. The l1-pitfall note names ～ないうちに (objective 2 and a checklist item both use that label) but illustrates it with 降っていないうちに, the ている-negative. That form does mean 'enquanto não está chovendo', which is precisely the reading the surrounding sentence denies, so the example argues against the note. 雨が降らないうちに is the canonical form for 'antes que comece a chover' and makes the note true. Tag multiset identical: <jp ...>, </jp>. One related gap is left for a human: the formation line still reads 'verbo na forma ている + うちに' and does not mention the ない form, which is a second anchor in the same field and cannot be covered by this single replacement.

Complaint confirmed and critical. In ex:tempo-01-3 (cloze) answer.text repeats the blanked prompt instead of holding the filler, so a learner who correctly types まで is graded wrong. The batch convention is filler-only: ex:n3-causa-08-3 stores text '料金' with full '空港で両替して、料金を払った。', and ex:n3-relato-02-1 stores text 'ない'. answer.full (疲れるまで走った) is already correct and is left untouched. Field path points at the leaf string inside the answer object, not the object itself. The mechanical applier missed it because it searched answer.correct and answer.choices, which a cloze exercise does not have.
